newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat drops to new lows on export competition.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat drops to new lows on export competition.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower and new contract lows were set with strong competition for exports leading the way down, traders said.
Traders said the price of U.S. wheat remains steep relative to other countries which continues to cut into potential export sales of U.S. supplies.
"U.S. wheat is too high priced relative to the EU and especially Argentina," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for Chicago-based grain house FIMAT Futures.
USDA early Monday said 20.419 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended October 17.
That's up from 18.668 million the previous week but is below the 30.924 million bu inspected the same week a year ago.
"The buyers (export) are few and far between, they just don't seem to have an appetite," Searcy said. "The funds are increasing their short positions as well."
Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each sold two million bushels of December, traders said.
The new contract low for March wheat is $3.92 per bushel, down from the previous low of $3.94 set Friday.
Wheat closed three to 4-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-1/4 at $4.00-1/2.
Traders agreed the supply of wheat in the United States wasn't burdensome and continued to tie the slide to contract lows to a lack of demand.

"There are no buyers. There's other origin wheat available and we're (U.S.) trying to decide whether or not we're going to have an export enhancement program or not. We keep threatening it," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Technical traders cited some encouragement for bulls that the December contract managed to close above support at $4.00 per bushel.
Also the near term nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed at 22.959 points, just above the 20 area which is considered a very oversold level.
But the four and 20 day moving averages for December continued to give off bearish signals and a lack of commercial demand for wheat on the way down left the market with a weak undertone.
Wheat futures volume according to the CBOT was estimated at 14,000, down from 19,512 Friday.
In wheat options, Refco Inc bought 100 December $3.90 puts at four cents and Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp sold 100 December $4.00 puts at 7-3/4 to eight cents.
Options volume was estimated at 5,000, down from 11,690 Friday.
